name: Cost Attribution and Budget Guards
question: Which feature, customer or run is spending the money, and what stops a runaway?
summary: The other techniques in this module lower the price of each call; this one makes spend visible and bounded. Every LLM call is tagged with who and what it serves (team, feature, customer, agent run, model), usually at a gateway, so the bill can be split by any tag and unit costs such as ₹ per invoice or per resolved ticket can be tracked. The same tags drive guards: a token or rupee budget per agent run that stops a looping agent, daily caps per customer or API key, alerts at a share of budget, and anomaly detection on spend per tag. Hard stops need care: a cap on a whole feature or on the account can halt real work for everyone.
useCases: Agent products where one run can loop for hours
Multi-tenant SaaS with free tiers or usage-based pricing
Finance asking which features and customers the LLM bill belongs to

items.detail: share of spend with team, feature, customer and run tags; aim above 95%
₹ per business outcome: per invoice drafted, per ticket resolved
tokens, rupees or steps per agent run, with a graceful stop
daily or monthly limits per tenant or API key
alerts at 50/80/100% of budget; spikes by tag against a baseline
legitimate work halted by caps set at too coarse a level

steps: Route all LLM calls through one gateway or SDK wrapper that requires tags
Report spend by feature, customer and run, and set unit-cost targets
Add per-run budgets and per-customer caps with clear user messages
Alert on budget thresholds and anomalies; review the top spenders weekly
pitfalls: Calls made directly to the provider that skip the gateway and its tags
A single account-wide hard cap that takes the whole product down
Budgets set in tokens while prices differ several-fold between models
remember: Tag every call; guard each run and each customer, not the whole account.

steps.title: Send every call through a gateway with tags
steps.text: Vyapar Sathi, a fictional small-business SaaS, routes all LLM calls through a LiteLLM proxy. Each call carries feature, customer and run tags, and calls without tags are rejected.

steps.title: Report spend by tag
steps.text: The bill of about ₹8,00,000 a month splits into GST invoice drafting 46%, the support agent 31%, reconciliation runs 15% and one free-tier customer 8%. Invoice drafting costs ₹1.40 per invoice.

steps.title: Budget each agent run
steps.text: A reconciliation run may spend ₹50. When a run loops, it stops with a clear message instead of running all night. Runaway loops had cost ₹1,20,000 a month.

steps.title: Cap each customer
steps.text: Each customer key has a daily budget. A free-tier account that scripted thousands of requests had cost ₹80,000 a month; its cap now stops it at ₹500 a day.

steps.title: Alert and detect spikes
steps.text: Alerts fire at 80% of a budget, and a daily job flags any tag whose spend is three times its usual level.

steps.title: Review the top spenders
steps.text: Each week the team reads the ten most expensive runs and customers. Waste falls from ₹2,00,000 to about ₹14,000 a month, with about 40 real runs stopped early.

practice.scenario: Vyapar Sathi, a fictional small-business SaaS for GST invoicing and bookkeeping, spent about ₹8,00,000 a month on LLM calls and could not say where it went. It routes every call through a LiteLLM gateway with feature, customer and run tags, finds that runaway reconciliation loops cost ₹1,20,000 a month and one scripted free-tier account ₹80,000, and adds a ₹50 budget per run, a ₹500 daily cap per customer key, alerts at 80% and spike detection. Waste falls to about ₹14,000 a month and invoice drafting is tracked at ₹1.40 per invoice.

library.name: LiteLLM
library.what: An OpenAI-compatible proxy with virtual keys, budgets per key, team or user, and spend tracking by tag.

practice.note: The proxy reads budgets from its database; set DATABASE_URL and a master key as in the LiteLLM docs. Prices per token are examples; load current prices for your models.

samples.code:
import litellm

PRICE_INR = {"claude-sonnet-5": (0.25 / 1000, 1.25 / 1000)}   # (input, output) per token, example

class BudgetExceeded(Exception):
    pass

class RunBudget:
    def __init__(self, run_id, max_inr=50.0):
        self.run_id, self.max_inr, self.spent = run_id, max_inr, 0.0

    def call(self, model, messages, **tags):
        if self.spent >= self.max_inr:
            raise BudgetExceeded(f"run {self.run_id} spent Rs {self.spent:.2f}")
        r = litellm.completion(model=model, messages=messages,
                               metadata={"tags": [f"{k}:{v}" for k, v in tags.items()] + [f"run:{self.run_id}"]})
        pin, pout = PRICE_INR[model]
        self.spent += r.usage.prompt_tokens * pin + r.usage.completion_tokens * pout
        return r

budget = RunBudget("recon-2026-09-27-0413")
reply = budget.call("claude-sonnet-5", [{"role": "user", "content": "Match these 40 UPI credits to invoices."}],
                    feature="reconciliation", customer="c-118")
print(round(budget.spent, 2))

interview.question: How would you find out where an LLM bill goes?
interview.answer: Route every call through a gateway or wrapper that requires tags for team, feature, customer and run, reject untagged calls, and report spend and unit cost by tag.

interview.question: How do you stop a runaway agent loop from costing a fortune?
interview.answer: Give each run a token or rupee budget checked before every call, stop gracefully with a clear message, alert at a share of the budget, and flag spend spikes per tag.
